theater.name: China / Taiwan
theater.title: China / Taiwan Strait and South China Sea
theater.sub: The options the US has toward China over Taiwan and the South China Sea, and what followed the last times the US did something like each one.
theater.proxy_note: Every reply here is an act by China itself (the PLA, the coast guard or the foreign ministry). Xinhua, Global Times, CGTN, PLA Daily and the Chinese defense and foreign ministries are used only as labelled claims of what China says. Routine PLA activity near Taiwan is background, not a reply, unless an allowed outlet ties it to a US move or it is a clear step up on a named day.
theater.hold_note: Option A is not built for China. A hold week would be a week with no US transit, arms sale, visit, sanction or talks, but the log is a sample of named events (2021 holds one row, and most FONOPs and allied drills are missing), and routine PLA flights near Taiwan happen almost daily and are not logged. A week that looks quiet may only be a week where nothing was logged, so NAPOR does not invent hold weeks.
theater.not_measured: Oil and chip prices, shipping and trade volumes, harm to ordinary Taiwanese and strain with allies are not measured. Only Chinese counter-sanctions and trade measures are.
theater.under_logged: The log is a sample of named events. 2021 and 2022-2023 US FONOPs are mostly missing, routine PLA flights are not logged, and some Chinese counter-sanctions were found only on outlets that are not allowed, so "none logged" is not proof nothing happened.
theater.claim_note: Chinese state media (Xinhua, Global Times, CGTN, PLA Daily)
theater.small_n: Small numbers: Taiwan-specific US moves are few. Most options here have only a handful of counted cases (the exact number is on each option), and options with fewer than 3 show "too few cases" instead of a percentage. Even the larger ones (D) are mostly cases where China answered with words and shadowing. Read every rate as a hint, not a forecast.

intensity.name: PLA activity level
intensity.note: PLA activity level counts logged Chinese drills, patrols, median-line crossings, coast-guard confrontations and missile launches in the 14 days before each date: 2 points each, +2 if someone died. Counter-sanctions are not counted. Routine daily PLA flights are not logged, so quiet stretches are understated.

act.verb: took a logged military or coast-guard action or a counter-sanction within 7 days
act.row: takes a military, coast-guard or counter-sanction action within 7 days

econ.name: Economic harm
econ.label: China answers with counter-sanctions or trade measures within 14 days

people.name: Harm to people
people.other: Share of past cases where anyone was reported hurt in a Chinese reply the log links to the move (or in the US move itself).
people.hold: Share of hold weeks in which a Chinese action in the 7 days after hurt anyone.

rule.other: Counts when anyone was reported hurt in a Chinese reply the log links to the move. Linked replies are usually within 7 days; for #3056 (Dec 2025 arms sale) the linked replies came on days 8 and 11 and are still checked here.
rule.hold: Counts when a Chinese action in the 7 days after the Monday hurt anyone.

escalation.name: Escalation
escalation.trigger: Share of past cases followed within 7 days by a named PLA drill, a spike in aircraft entering Taiwan's air defense zone, a coast-guard confrontation or a Chinese counter-sanction that China or an allowed outlet ties to the US move. Routine flights and shadowing do not count.
escalation.other: Share of past cases followed within 7 days by any logged Chinese military or coast-guard action (a drill, patrol, median-line crossing, close pass, deployment, missile launch or coast-guard confrontation) or counter-sanction (timing only).
escalation.hold: Share of hold weeks followed within 7 days by any logged Chinese military or coast-guard action (a drill, patrol, median-line crossing, close pass, deployment, missile launch or coast-guard confrontation) or counter-sanction (timing only).

rule.trigger: Counts when China replied within 7 days with a named PLA drill, an air-defense-zone spike, a coast-guard confrontation or a counter-sanction that China or an allowed outlet ties to the US move (Trigger Census status R-strong or R-weak). Routine flights and shadowing do not count.
rule.other: Counts when the log holds any logged Chinese military or coast-guard action (a drill, patrol, median-line crossing, close pass, deployment, missile launch or coast-guard confrontation) or counter-sanction in the 7 days after the move (timing only, not shown to be a reply). Unlike the reply rule, a patrol or close pass counts here.

military.name: Military cost
military.reply: Share of past cases where China's reply was a live-fire drill or a named large-scale drill.
military.strike: Share of hold weeks with a live-fire or named large-scale Chinese drill in the 7 days after.
military.none: No direct military cost expected from the move itself, so this counts as 0%.

rule.reply: Counts when a Chinese reply the log links to the move was a live-fire or named large-scale drill. Combat patrols, median-line crossings, a close pass at sea and a coast-guard confrontation do not. Linked replies are usually within 7 days, but not always: the Justice Mission 2025 drills came 11 days after the Dec 18, 2025 arms sale (#3056) and count here, although the escalation corner (7 days) counts #3056 as no reply.
rule.strike: Counts when a live-fire or named large-scale Chinese drill took place in the 7 days after the Monday.

economic.name: Economic harm
economic.other: Share of past cases followed within 14 days by Chinese counter-sanctions or trade measures against US firms or the US (timing only, not shown to be caused by the US move).
economic.rule: Counts when China announced counter-sanctions or trade measures against US firms or the US within 14 days after the move.

political.name: Political / diplomatic
political.other: Share of past cases NOT followed by talks or leader contact within 14 days.
political.rule: Counts when no talks or leader contact (a call, a summit or a senior meeting, by anyone) was logged within 14 days after the move.

hostile.title: Formations of J-10 and J-11 fighters briefly cross to Taiwan's side shortly before Azar meets Tsai; Taiwan's MND says they were tracked and 'driven out' and calls it deliberate. No aircraft count given

A US defense official tells Reuters China launched four medium-range ballistic missiles into the South China Sea. The timing against the Entity List announcement is unclear and China did not link them. A day earlier China had complained about a US U-2 over a live-fire zone
Chinese aircraft cross the Strait again while the US envoy is in Taiwan (headline only; no count was read)

China says more than 100 warplanes and 10 warships took part in the first two days; Chinese state media say missiles were fired over Taiwan (Japan says five landed in its exclusive economic zone and four others flew over Taiwan). Al Jazeera says the PLA kept drilling on Aug 8, past the planned Aug 7 end

China's three-day drills simulate sealing off the island. Taiwan's MND reports 91 Chinese aircraft on Monday Apr 10, 54 crossing the median line (AFP). AFP ties the drills to the Tsai-McCarthy meeting

A Chinese guided-missile destroyer crosses the Chung-Hoon's bow at about 150 yards (US Indo-Pacific Command); the Chung-Hoon slows to 10 knots. China's defense minister Li Shangfu says the US and allies created the danger

China's Eastern Theater Command calls the drills a 'stern warning' to Taiwan separatists colluding with outside forces. Taiwan's MND: 42 aircraft since 9 a.m., 26 crossing the median line, 8 ships (Bloomberg)

The command announces 'joint naval and air combat patrols' the same day as the allied drill; AFP calls its line about 'hotspots' an apparent swipe at the allied drills. The Philippine military saw two Chinese ships that did not interfere
Drills start three days after Lai Ching-te's inauguration, in which he urged Beijing to stop 'intimidation'. No US move is named as the trigger

Chinese vessels block a Philippine resupply run to the BRP Sierra Madre; a Philippine sailor is severely injured and boats damaged. The Pentagon condemns 'escalatory and irresponsible actions'. China's coast guard blames Manila. The US had restated in March that the defense treaty covers Philippine coast guard vessels

China frames the drills as a reply to Lai's Oct 10 National Day speech. Taiwan's MND: 125 sorties, 90 entering the ADIZ, 17 PLA Navy and 17 coast guard ships. The Pentagon calls it 'irresponsible, disproportionate, and destabilizing'

hostile.actor: China (PLA / coast guard, per Taiwan MND)
hostile.title: Taiwan's defense ministry reports the largest Chinese maritime movements in decades and 47 PLA aircraft in 24 hours; Beijing announced no drills and did not acknowledge it. This is day 10 after the Lai transit began

Taiwan's MND reports 32 sorties, 22 crossing the median line, plus live fire. USNI names no trigger; China's foreign ministry says it is 'not a question related to foreign affairs'. This is day 16 after the Feb 10 transit

Taiwan's MND counts 76 aircraft, 15 PLA Navy ships and 4 official ships in 24 hours, with 37 sorties crossing the median line into the ADIZ. China's defense ministry blames Lai's 'independence' provocations; USNI names no US trigger
About 10 nautical miles off Scarborough Shoal, China Coast Guard cutter 3104 collides with PLA Navy destroyer Guilin while both chase the Philippine ship

Eastern Theater Command blockade-style drills with live-fire. Taiwan reports 89 aircraft and drone sorties with 67 in the ADIZ, 14 PLA Navy ships and 14 coast guard ships and a 4-ship amphibious group on day one. USNI says the drills protested the arms sales

Maritime authorities announce live-fire drills on Jul 23-24 in two areas within about 7 miles of the Chinese coast. Reuters notes they follow the Rubio-Wang talks the day before and gives no stated reason; this is treated as background

The Philippines accuses China of using water cannon on its vessels on Jul 23 and 24 at Scarborough Shoal (a separate confrontation at Second Thomas Shoal the Monday before). Rubio, in Manila, calls China's actions 'disturbing' and reaffirms support
